public_rationale: The statement has no deadline and appears as one branch of an either-or claim. The reviewed evidence establishes financing activity, not cash exhaustion or permanent solvency. No decisive event was found by October 28. The claim cannot fairly be marked false merely because OpenAI had not yet run out of money, or true because reports forecast future cash pressure.
limitations: The alternative branch has no defined measure of size and success.
Financing received does not establish remaining cash.
The unspecified accounting basis prevents a decisive quantitative money comparison.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI has only two possible outcomes: it becomes the largest and most successful company of all time, or it runs out of money at some point.

our_interpretation: The sentence is one branch of an either-or statement, not an unconditional prediction of bankruptcy.
Runs out of money means an inability to meet due obligations because usable cash and available financing are exhausted.
Accounting losses, negative cash flow and projections of future cash exhaustion do not by themselves meet that condition.

criteria.support_condition: A documented cash-exhaustion event establishes the financially testable branch of the disjunction. Establishing the alternative branch would require a defensible interpretation of both largest and most successful.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A terminal outcome, such as a solvent wind-down, establishes that OpenAI neither exhausted its funding nor achieved the claimed exceptional scale. Ordinary continued operation cannot disprove an unlimited eventuality.
